claims.statement: NeuroPixel represents a recurrent neural state on a spatial canvas updated by a learned local residual rule, s[t+1] = s[t] + W2 ReLU(W1 concat(s[t], K*s[t], u) + b1) + b2, with a learned depthwise 3x3 perception K, a learned seed, an RGB retina for identity channels and a shared projection/dictionary decoder; it is implemented in PyTorch and in three graphics backends: a scalar RGBA32F fragment renderer, a four-channel vector fragment renderer and an OpenGL 4.6 compute backend with SSBO weights and shared pixel tiles.
claims.population: The NeuroPixel software in this repository (PyTorch model and three OpenGL backends)
limits: Implementation description only; not a biological brain or a complete causal explanation
The scanner applies the decoder beyond the supervised output cell; semantic correctness at every displayed cell is not established
Learned cellular updates and GPU/WebGL image execution have primary antecedents (Mordvintsev et al., 2020); no priority is claimed
Memory and rest-state behaviour shown in pre-scientific figures are not established by current evidence
No independent laboratory replication and no externally dated public preregistration

claims.statement: Graphics execution reproduces the neural computation within the registered checks: the extended fragment preflight passed 136 physical RTX 3090 checks (states, masks, retina, logits and decisions); learned deployment reproduced all 320 tested decisions of the five selected visual models (first 64 official test rows each) against native CUDA and original CPU predictions; the Torch-free compute preflight passed 21 checks across seven workloads.
claims.population: The NeuroPixel software in this repository (PyTorch model and three OpenGL backends); RTX 3090, FP32
limits: Engineering validations on fixed subsets, not new training realizations or outside replications
Pointwise logit and mean NLL limits as registered; no claim beyond the tested rows
No independent laboratory replication and no externally dated public preregistration

claims.statement: The interactive VIS07 viewer exposes all sixteen raw channels, an RGB projection, per-cell decoder probabilities and reset/depth controls; archive mode passed 50 HTTP checks and browser controls, live physical GPU integration passed 27 trajectory gates plus 52 HTTP checks including the ten TRAIN resets, and a separate CPU/Mesa execution passed the same internal endpoint.
claims.population: VIS07 viewer software on the RTX 3090 host and a separate CPU/Mesa runner
limits: Software integration checks; not evidence of semantic interpretability
No independent laboratory replication and no externally dated public preregistration

claims.statement: The README animations are captures of actual model states linked by SHA-256 in docs/animations/manifest.json, not synthetic artwork; the trained-trajectory GIF is an actual GPU-rendered capture of the selected VIS07 model (registered seed 240, fixed TRAIN digit 0), slowed for inspection, with colours projecting raw channels.

claims.population: VIS07 main cohort, five paired seeds
limits: Excludes installation, scheduling, compilation, transfers, storage and verification; no energy measurement
No independent laboratory replication and no externally dated public preregistration

Formal proof rebuilding is a separate gate (task M3)
